title: 6 Best SQLite Frontend Builders in 2026
summary: Six ways to build a frontend on SQLite, from publishing a read-only site to building forms and internal tools other people can use.
body_markdown:
SQLite runs inside a lot of small products, prototypes and edge deployments. At some point someone who is not a developer needs to see or change what is in the file. A SQL client is fine for the developer; everyone else needs a frontend with search, forms and limits on what they can touch.


Below are six SQLite frontend builders, with the point where each one stops. For desktop clients, see the[best SQLite GUI tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-sqlite-gui-tools/) .


## What a SQLite frontend needs to do


- Reach the database. SQLite is a file, so the tool either runs next to it or reaches it through a server or hosted SQLite service.
- Give non-developers search, filters and forms instead of SQL.
- Limit who can edit which tables.
- Keep writes safe, since SQLite allows one writer at a time.

## The options


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to SQLite and builds a frontend on your tables: lists with search and filters, record pages, forms and dashboards. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or in code. Data stays in your database.


Each person signs in and sees only the tables and actions their role allows. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it is not a SQL client for schema changes or query tuning.


### 2. Datasette


Datasette turns a SQLite file into a browsable website and JSON API, with faceted search and saved queries. It is a good fit for publishing data.


**Where it stops:** editing and authentication need plugins, and it is not built for workflows.


### 3. NocoDB


NocoDB puts a spreadsheet-style interface on SQL databases, including SQLite, with grid, form and kanban views.


**Where it stops:** custom logic and multi-step processes are limited.


### 4. Streamlit


Streamlit lets a Python developer build a data app on SQLite in a single script.


**Where it stops:** every screen and permission is code you maintain.


### 5. Retool


Retool supports SQLite through a connected server or resource, and developers build screens from components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** developer-built, with per-user pricing.


### 6. Appsmith


Appsmith is an open-source internal tool builder you can self-host next to the database.


**Where it stops:** expect JavaScript for anything past basic CRUD.


## Which to use


- **A team needs to view and edit SQLite data safely, without code:** Jet Admin.
- **You want to publish a dataset as a website:** Datasette.
- **People want a spreadsheet view:** NocoDB.
- **A Python developer wants a quick data app:** Streamlit.
- **Developers will build and maintain the tool:** Retool or Appsmith.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can a web frontend work with a SQLite file?


Yes, if the frontend can reach the file through a server, or you use a hosted SQLite service. A browser cannot open a file on your laptop directly.


### Is SQLite fine for multi-user apps?


For internal tools with moderate write traffic, usually yes. Many concurrent writers is where you move to Postgres or MySQL.
